cards.title: Segment or consolidate — a two-brand worked example
cards.summary: Two brands at the same revenue and margin can need opposite structures because SKU count, persona count and region complexity differ.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of a store's commercial complexity should be reflected in the paid account structure.

cards.title: Control existing-customer spend and frequency
cards.summary: Allocate a deliberate, low, frequency-capped budget to existing customers instead of letting cold campaigns accidentally retarget them.
cards.use_when: Setting retention spend and exclusions across a store's paid social acquisition campaigns.

cards.title: Log these four account-level mistakes at low spend
cards.summary: Common low-spend errors: testing inside the scaling campaign, skipping exclusions, killing tests too early, and over-budgeting adsets via the 50-conversion rule.
cards.use_when: Auditing a small store's paid social account before restructuring or scaling.

cards.title: Concept Matrix: Persona × Angle × Offer × Ad Type
cards.summary: Build ad concepts as persona/angle/offer/ad-type combinations so each ad set tests a readable, nicheable concept rather than a random batch of creative.
cards.use_when: Structuring acquisition campaigns and ad sets for a store, deciding how to brief creative, or diagnosing why you can't tell which audience message is winning.

cards.title: Ad Volume Targets and Ad-to-Ad-Set Ratio at Scale
cards.summary: High-spend stores should launch roughly 100–300 new ads per month, which is manageable inside a small number of campaigns and ad sets.
cards.use_when: Planning monthly creative production and deciding how many campaigns and ad sets your account needs to absorb that output.

cards.title: Plan advertising continuity and test bid strategies within permitted account use
cards.summary: Separate operational continuity from experiments intended to find incremental profitable demand.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to open a second ad account when a store is heavily reliant on one platform for new customer acquisition.

cards.title: International Expansion Without Ad-Account Sprawl
cards.summary: Keep country targeting inside one ad account and only split accounts when you have a real reason such as local-currency billing.
cards.use_when: Planning to sell into new regions and deciding whether each region needs its own ad account or just separate targeting and reporting rules.

cards.title: Five-Campaign Account Structure for ~$750K/Month Spend
cards.summary: A worked example of a high-spend account: testing, scaling, promo, advertorial and DPA campaigns each with a distinct job.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the campaign-level architecture of a store spending in the high six to seven figures monthly.

cards.title: What Stays Fixed as Spend Scales
cards.summary: Four fundamentals — data integrity, commercial alignment, the concept framework, and ad-set/campaign KPI-ing — should never be traded away when adding account layers.
cards.use_when: Auditing a complex high-spend account or deciding whether a new structural element is worth adding.

cards.title: ABO vs CBO: Choose Your Risk/Efficiency Profile
cards.summary: ABO vs CBO is a risk-vs-efficiency trade-off, not a right answer, and seasonal rotation between them is a legitimate tactic.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to distribute spend across new creative tests, especially in peak vs testing seasons.

cards.title: Ad Set Composition: 3 to 15 Ads, Same Audience
cards.summary: Keep a minimum of three ads per ad set so they can sequence, and keep every ad in the ad set resonating with the same audience.
cards.use_when: Building ad sets and deciding how many creative assets to place in each one.

cards.title: Consolidate Funnel Stages in One Ad Set to Avoid Biased Readouts
cards.summary: Consolidating top-, mid- and bottom-of-funnel ads in a single ad set makes the concept easier to read than splitting them by awareness stage.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to split a persona's ads by stage of awareness at the ad-set level, or keep them grouped.

cards.title: Name Ad Sets by Persona, Angle, Offer, Content Type, Date
cards.summary: Structured ad-set naming is what makes it possible to filter, bundle and KPI concepts across a campaign after the fact.
cards.use_when: Setting up ad sets or cleaning up an inherited account where you need concept-level reporting.

cards.title: Retargeting Is a Capped Support Layer, Not a Growth Driver
cards.summary: Treat retargeting with a scarcity mindset — minimise spend, consolidate audiences, and manage by frequency and profitability rather than percentage of budget.
cards.use_when: Auditing retargeting and existing-customer spend allocation in an ad account.

cards.title: DPAs Only Look Great Because They Sit at the Point of Purchase
cards.summary: DPA ROAS is inflated by last-click position, and DPA performance is a direct reflection of top-of-funnel investment — starving the top causes a DPA death spiral.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much to spend on dynamic product ads and whether to cut creative/top-of-funnel budget because DPA ROAS looks strong.

cards.title: Budget Existing-Customer Spend in Dollars, Not as a Percentage
cards.summary: Percentage-of-spend targets for existing customers are the wrong frame; decide by profitability and by a dollar budget derived from customers × CPM × desired frequency.
cards.use_when: Setting existing-customer and retargeting budget for a period, or reviewing whether a spend-cap percentage is meaningful.

cards.title: Settings to Turn Off: Flexible Ads, One-Day View, Auto Creative Optimisations
cards.summary: Disable settings that destroy readout clarity or shift budget attribution — flexible ads, one-day view attribution in decisions, and Advantage+ creative auto-optimisations at both ad and advertiser level.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning a store's ad account settings and creative configuration.

cards.title: Maintain Audience Segment Sync Audit (CRM → Meta)
cards.summary: Periodically verify that the CRM-to-Meta audience segment sync hasn't broken, otherwise existing customers get treated as new and spend integrity erodes.
cards.use_when: During routine account audits; especially after third-party tooling or CRM changes.

cards.title: Calculate Test Budget from Conversions, CPA and Duration
cards.summary: Set test budgets by defining the statistical threshold and the learning window first, then dividing threshold × expected CPA by days.
cards.use_when: Planning a creative or concept test and sizing the daily budget so it reaches a conclusion in the timeframe you chose.

cards.title: Creative as the Growth Lever, Portfolio Model Over Hero Ads
cards.summary: Meta has compressed media-buying arbitrage and left creative as the leverage point; diversify spend across many ads rather than betting on a few winners that will fatigue.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of the store's investment goes into creative production vs media-buying tactics, and how to manage creative risk.

cards.title: Diagnose Creative Bottlenecks Before Adding Volume
cards.summary: Name which creative bottleneck is actually constraining growth — quality, format diversity, funnel-stage coverage, partnership ads, or strategy — before spending more on volume.
cards.use_when: When creative output is high but growth is flat or unprofitable, or before deciding what to change in the creative system.

cards.title: How Andromeda Reversed Targeting: Ads Go In, Meta Finds the Audience
cards.summary: In the source's simplification, pre-Andromeda you chose an interest then loaded creative; post-Andromeda you load creative with no targeting and Meta infers the audience from the ads themselves.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much effort to put into interest/audience targeting versus into the content of the creative itself.

cards.title: Post-Andromeda account structure: creative as targeting
cards.summary: Meta's algorithm now infers audience from creative content, so ad account structure should lead with diverse concepts rather than interest targeting.
cards.use_when: Structuring or restructuring Meta ad account campaigns for a store, deciding whether to keep interest targeting, or diagnosing wasted spend.

cards.title: Creative similarity, frequency and reach decay
cards.summary: Near-duplicate creatives get bundled and served to the same pool, raising frequency, shrinking net-new reach and depressing ROAS over time.
cards.use_when: Planning creative volume and variety for a Meta campaign, or diagnosing rising frequency and falling reach on a store's cold traffic campaigns.

cards.title: Creative sequencing and why not to kill low-ROAS ads
cards.summary: Ads work as an ordered sequence, but attribution is last-click, so the ad that appears to convert is often not the ad that started the journey.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Meta ad-level ROAS to decide whether to pause or scale individual creatives in a store's account.

cards.title: Metric reliability by account level
cards.summary: ROAS reliability increases as you move from ad to ad set to campaign, with campaign-level numbers closest to P&L under specific reporting conditions.
cards.use_when: Choosing which metric level to use when judging store acquisition performance or deciding whether a creative or campaign should continue.

cards.title: Four components of concept diversity
cards.summary: Concept diversity comes from varying persona, angle, offer and format, and the same creative set should be judged on which of these actually changed.
cards.use_when: Briefing new creative batches or deciding what to vary when scaling a store's Meta creative library.

cards.title: Persona construction: archetypes not demographics
cards.summary: Build narrow problem-defined personas rather than demographic buckets so creative briefs contain enough specificity to hold spend.
cards.use_when: Doing customer and audience research to feed ad creative, PDP messaging or email segmentation for a store.

cards.title: Building an angle: assemble the components that fit the persona
cards.summary: An angle is the specific argument used with a persona, assembled from problem agitation, contrarian framing, proof, curiosity and objection handling.
cards.use_when: Writing ad scripts, hooks or landing page copy for a specific store audience.

cards.title: Testing priority order: angle before offer, persona or format
cards.summary: When creative is underperforming, the source prioritizes fixing the angle before testing offer, persona or format, because angle defects are the common root cause.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a store's underperforming acquisition and deciding what to change in the next creative test.

cards.title: Structuring ad sets by concept for a usable learning loop
cards.summary: One concept per ad set preserves interpretable results and prevents the ad set from receiving mixed audience signals.
cards.use_when: Setting up or reorganizing a store's Meta campaign structure before a creative test cycle.

cards.title: Worked concept build: persona, angle, offer, format
cards.summary: A full concept example shows how to chain persona income, proof type, specific outcome and offer framing into one brief.
cards.use_when: Briefing a new creative set for a supplement or physical-product store and needing a repeatable template.

cards.title: Hooks as relevance promises, not bait
cards.summary: A hook's job is to signal relevance and context to the right viewer, not to trick anyone into watching.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the first three seconds of paid video or static ads for a store, and allocating production time between hooks and bodies.

cards.title: Hook grading criteria and reusable hook types
cards.summary: Grade hooks on clarity, relevance, novelty, specificity and credibility, and pull from proven hook archetypes.
cards.use_when: Reviewing drafts of ad hooks or landing page headlines for a store before production spend.

cards.title: Scroll-stopping hook mechanisms and when each works
cards.summary: Nine hook archetypes for paid and organic creative, with the awareness stage each one resonates with.
cards.use_when: Writing the first 3 seconds of acquisition creative (Meta/TikTok/YouTube) or organic content, and deciding which hook angle to test for a given audience.

cards.title: Bridge scripting: never jump from hook to product
cards.summary: The hook-to-body and body-to-CTA bridges are where most ads break; introduce the product gradually instead of abruptly.
cards.use_when: Scripting or editing video ads (and writing paid social copy) where the product appears mid-creative and you need to keep viewers from feeling suddenly sold to.

cards.title: Hook testing still works post-Andromeda — and it's cheap
cards.summary: Changing only the first 3 seconds produces a distinct Meta creative ID that gets its own audience and can resurrect fatigued winners.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep investing in hook variations versus building entirely new concepts, especially when a proven ad has fatigued.

cards.title: Five questions to choose the right ad format
cards.summary: Define concept first, then decide format by education need, single-frame communicability, product demo need, and awareness stage.
cards.use_when: Planning a creative production batch for a product or persona — deciding video vs static vs carousel before briefing production.

cards.title: Cost of production versus contribution margin per ad — the image vs video decision
cards.summary: Calculate average contribution margin per ad against cost of producing it, split by format, to decide where to double down.
cards.use_when: Allocating creative production budget between images and video, or diagnosing why an ad account isn't scaling despite decent ad performance.

cards.title: Advertorial statics: make the ad look like an organic post
cards.summary: Advertorial static ads work by mimicking platform-native content formats and only revealing the sale in the copy, paired with an educational landing experience.
cards.use_when: Designing top-of-funnel static creative for cold audiences, especially in health/wellness or older demographics.

cards.title: Review/round-up advertorial funnel with a dermatologist framing
cards.summary: A 'best products of the year' review article run through a doctor's page, ranking competitors badly and the brand best, feeding a quiz funnel.
cards.use_when: Building a top-of-funnel static ad plus education page for a product with many alternatives and authority-driven demand (hair growth, supplements, skincare).

cards.title: Long-form copy statics for 50+ demographics
cards.summary: Static image ads with very long copy that pull an unaware audience through all awareness stages perform strongly on Facebook feeds for 50+ audiences.
cards.use_when: Building cold-audience creative for an older target demographic where long copy and story-based education can convert.

cards.title: VSSL script structure: persona call-out, objection handling, problem agitation, then late product reveal
cards.summary: How to run a video sales letter that educates and handles objections before introducing the product.
cards.use_when: Scripting a video sales letter or long-form educational ad for a problem/solution category like supplements or health.

cards.title: Objection-handling UGC spliced onto the front of a VSSL
cards.summary: A proven VSSL format with contrarian takes and split-screen engagement, plus objection-handling UGC at the front.
cards.use_when: Producing long-form video ads for cold audiences where you want to keep people watching via contrarian framing before an educational body.

cards.title: Incremental attribution: read DPA ROAS correctly before scaling bottom of funnel
cards.summary: DPAs show inflated attributed ROAS because they credit existing customers and non-incremental conversions; use incremental attribution to see the real number.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much budget to put into DPA/carousel retargeting, particularly in fashion, and evaluating whether bottom-of-funnel is scalable on cold audiences.

cards.title: Allocate creative effort by funnel need with a normalized budget
cards.summary: Prioritize acquisition creative while protecting useful objection-handling and retention work.
cards.use_when: Planning how many top, middle, and bottom of funnel creative assets to produce in the next cycle, and where to focus budget.

cards.title: Partnership ads: using creator audience data for cold targeting
cards.summary: Ads run through the creator's handle use both handles' audience data to find new cold users and feel more authentic.
cards.use_when: Choosing whether to invest in creator collaborations or whitelisting/partnership ads and how heavily to weight them in the account.

cards.title: Testing cycle: hypothesis, volume, launch, analyze, scale, iterate
cards.summary: How to run a creative testing cycle given a typical hit rate, including how many ads to make per concept.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new creative test for a concept, or deciding how many ads are needed before judging whether a concept works.

cards.title: When to add ads to an adset vs launch a new adset
cards.summary: Don't disrupt a winning adset's learning phase; if it's below KPI, change anything you want.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to add new creative to an existing adset or create a new adset, based on whether the adset is hitting KPI.

cards.title: Metrics ranked by reliability for judging creative
cards.summary: Amount spent is the best proxy for creative performance, followed by 7-day click or incremental ROAS/CPA, then CPC/CTR, with hook and hold rates as diagnostics only.
cards.use_when: Reviewing creative performance in the ad account to decide which ads to scale, cut, or iterate on.

cards.title: ABO vs CBO: risk tolerance trade-off via Pareto's principle
cards.summary: CBO concentrates spend into a tiny share of ads, improving efficiency but raising fatigue and portfolio risk; ABO de-risks but typically at slightly lower ROI.
cards.use_when: Choosing campaign budgeting method for a product portfolio, or deciding when to switch to CBO to spike efficiency.

cards.title: Fix the 90/10 desire vs pain-point creative imbalance
cards.summary: Many large retailers skew creative toward campaign-shoot desire imagery and under-invest in pain-point-led performance assets.
cards.use_when: Auditing existing creative mix, especially for a retailer with a legacy campaign shoot process, and rebalancing production budgets toward performance assets.

cards.title: Bottom-of-funnel retargeting as objection handling
cards.summary: Model why the 95% of site visitors who didn't buy didn't buy, and build retargeting creative to answer each objection type.
cards.use_when: Building bottom-of-funnel retargeting for a product or category, and diagnosing why retargeting creative is underperforming.

cards.title: Diagnose bottom-of-funnel objections before writing BOF creative
cards.summary: Segment non-buyers into price, trust, quality and timing objections, then match each to a specific bottom-of-funnel creative treatment.
cards.use_when: Planning retargeting and bottom-of-funnel ad creative for shoppers who visited the store or PDP but did not purchase.

cards.title: Creative volume hierarchy: volume beats concept, hook and editing
cards.summary: Rank creative production priorities as volume, concept quality, hook strength, editing, UGC talent, storytelling — and target a minimum quality bar rather than guessing winners.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest limited ad-production effort and headcount across hooks, concepts, editing and creators.

cards.title: Calculate creative volume from spend or from hit-rate back-propagation
cards.summary: Use $1,000 monthly ad spend per new ad as a quick rule, or back-propagate required volume from average spend per ad, expected revenue and new-customer revenue targets.
cards.use_when: Setting how many new creatives to brief per month for a given ad budget or new-customer revenue target.

cards.title: Set the creative production budget as a share of media spend by scale
cards.summary: Allocate 0% cash (founder time) at 4–30K/month, 25% of media budget to production at 30–100K/month, and ~10% above 100K/month.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much budget to put into creative production versus ad distribution at your current monthly spend level.

cards.title: Treat creative as a revenue driver, not a cost centre: the redistribution math
cards.summary: Model the efficiency gain from moving ad budget into production versus running too few ads, and avoid the failure mode of scaling a starved account.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to shift spend from distribution channels into creative production when the account has few active ads relative to spend.

cards.title: Test creative volume cheaply with trial reels before ad manager
cards.summary: Post ad cutdowns as trial reels with the CTA removed to get view data and retention graphs, then only push the best hooks into the ad account.
cards.use_when: Choosing which hooks or early-cut creative to fund with paid spend, or iterating on a video before final production.

cards.title: Understand creative fatigue as spend capacity plus audience size
cards.summary: Every ad has a finite lifetime spend capacity; fatigue comes from either the asset going stale or the targeted audience being too small.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to push a winning ad harder, introduce replacements, or re-target a narrow persona.

cards.title: Match persona breadth to spend capacity; go specific first, broad later
cards.summary: Narrow persona callouts cap daily spend capacity; broader audiences scale further but demand stronger creative — start specific, expand at scale.
cards.use_when: Choosing how specific the persona callout in an ad script should be, or deciding when to broaden targeting to scale spend.

cards.title: Recover spend from fatiguing ads with four tactics
cards.summary: Iterate hooks, move ads to cost-cap campaigns, re-use post IDs in scaling campaigns, or translate formats to extract more spend from a decaying winner.
cards.use_when: Extending a winning ad's life before turning it off or replacing it.

cards.title: Run portfolio management across ads, products and the balance sheet
cards.summary: Above ~$50K/month, treat media buying as risk diversification across ads and products, and reconcile P&L optimisation with balance-sheet/inventory reality.
cards.use_when: Setting media buying priorities when running a large ad account, especially if unsold inventory is accumulating or efficiency targets conflict with sell-through.

cards.title: Budget creative effort across replication, iteration and net-new
cards.summary: Allocate roughly 50–60% to replicating winners, 20–30% to iterating underperformers, and 20–30% to net-new concepts — most brands over-weight net-new.
cards.use_when: Planning a monthly creative production calendar and deciding which types of assets to brief.

cards.title: Brief creators with their past work plus the brief behind it
cards.summary: Creator output quality follows brief quality; assess a creator by comparing what they produced against the brief they were given.
cards.use_when: Sourcing and briefing UGC creators or agencies for ecommerce ad production.

cards.title: Build the creative production team by spend tier
cards.summary: Hire a video editor, static designer and creative strategist (plus creators) in a tiered structure matched to monthly ad spend.
cards.use_when: Planning creative production headcount and roles for an ecommerce ad account as spend scales.

cards.title: Automate the middle of the creative process with AI, not the ends
cards.summary: Apply AI heavily to briefing and script writing and to production, but not to ideation or final analysis.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to insert LLM/AI tooling into your creative production workflow.

cards.title: Match persona callouts and creative to audience warmth and account scale
cards.summary: Use broad audience creative only if you can sustain it; start content-first and video-heavy, and match creative to the awareness stage.
cards.use_when: Setting the targeting and creative approach for a new or growing ecommerce brand.

cards.title: Google Ads structure: consolidation beats segmentation, unless commercial reality forces segmentation
cards.summary: Merge low-data campaigns into consolidated ones so the algorithm learns from more conversions, and only split out for commercial necessity (clearance, new arrivals).
cards.use_when: Restructuring an ecommerce Google Ads account that is fragmented into many campaigns with low conversion volumes.

cards.title: Recognise Google spend as either over-spending or under-spending
cards.summary: Google sits bottom-of-funnel and captures existing demand at high ROAS, which leads to two opposite errors: pushing spend that isn't incremental, or refusing to scale when cold search demand exists.
cards.use_when: Auditing Google Ads spend levels and deciding whether to increase, hold or decrease budget.

cards.title: Apply the five major Google Ads shifts when restructuring in 2026
cards.summary: Account for PMAX's ceiling, standard shopping's return, changed match-type definitions, AIMAX/demand gen, and DSA deprecation before rebuilding the account.
cards.use_when: Revisiting a Google Ads account built on older playbooks or when PMAX stops scaling.

cards.title: Justify every campaign beyond one (justification-based account structure)
cards.summary: Build Google Ads accounts around one default consolidated campaign and require a commercial justification for each added campaign.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the account structure for a store's Google Shopping/Search program and deciding whether to split into more campaigns.

cards.title: Route 80-90% of ecommerce spend to Shopping, not Search
cards.summary: Ecommerce and retail accounts should put most spend into Shopping because pre-click information improves traffic quality.
cards.use_when: Deciding budget allocation between Shopping and Search campaigns for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Use single-topic ad groups (STAG) instead of SKAGs
cards.summary: Replace single-keyword ad groups with themed ad groups holding 10-20 related keywords and theme-tuned ads.
cards.use_when: Building or restructuring Search campaign ad groups for a store's keyword themes.

cards.title: Structure PMax asset groups by product type with matched listing groups
cards.summary: Build 3-20 PMax asset groups segmented by product type, each with its own customized listing group of at least 15 products.
cards.use_when: Setting up or fixing a Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce catalog.

cards.title: Diagnose why PMax segmentation is worth breaking consolidation
cards.summary: Use four concrete benefits to decide whether splitting PMax asset groups is justified for a store.
cards.use_when: Justifying or rejecting PMax asset-group segmentation for a specific product category set.

cards.title: Set brand exclusions (two ways) on PMax to stop pure retargeting
cards.summary: Always exclude branded traffic from PMax so the campaign cannot over-credit warm/repeat conversions.
cards.use_when: Configuring PMax campaigns and auditing whether brand traffic is inflating reported ROAS.

cards.title: Run feed-only PMax to force Shopping placement and fix runaway spend
cards.summary: Delete asset groups to create a feed-only PMax that can only serve Shopping + Display retargeting, controlling misrouted spend.
cards.use_when: When PMax is over-spending on Gmail/YouTube or you want to force spend into Shopping placement.

cards.title: Move to tROAS for stability, then avoid the over-tightening trap
cards.summary: Start on max conversion value for data, roll into target ROAS for day-to-day reliability, and watch for the tROAS trap of throttling cold reach.
cards.use_when: Choosing and tuning a bidding strategy for a store's PMax/Shopping campaigns.

cards.title: Build a feeder strategy: cold funnel campaign feeding a high-tROAS retargeter
cards.summary: Run a very low-tROAS cold campaign to cheaply reach under-bid auctions, then convert that traffic with a high-tROAS campaign.
cards.use_when: When you need genuine cold acquisition in Google that PMax over-attributes on its own.
